newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian police arrest 100 Shi'ite Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian police arrest 100 Shi'ite Moslems.

text.p: Nigerian police have arrested 100 men at a mosque on suspicion of belonging to the fundamentalist Shi'ite Moslem Brothers and calling for the abolition of the government, a police spokesman said on Thursday.
"We picked them up on Wednesday at a gathering in a mosque," police spokesman Umar Shelleng told Reuters by telephone from northern Sokoto state where the arrests took place.
"They were into subversive preachings, calling for the abolition of the present government and installation of an Islamic one...threatening national security," he added.

The outlawed Moslem Brothers group is campaigning for imposition of Islamic Sharia law in Africa's most populous nation, although only about half the 100 million people are Moslems, mainly of the Sunni sect.
Shelleng said this was the third arrest in the town since December of people suspected of being members of the group.
"This batch of 100 are in detention and will face charges of incitement and disturbance of public peace, illegal preachings and unlawful assembly," he said.
Last week, a Sokoto area court gave bail to 15 people charged with similar offences for lack of evidence. It adjourned the case of 28 others to next Wednesday.

In September, two policemen and five Shi'ites were killed in northern Nigeria when supporters of the Moslem Brothers group clashed with the police while demanding the release of their arrested leader, Sheikh Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak-Zaky.
El-Zak-Zaky, a radical preacher, was arrested because of illegal publications and radio broadcasts, the police said. He was also alleged to have imported arms.
